messages:
Maya (Head of Strategy): Thanks all — quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Drop any strategy / positioning / roadmap Qs here. I'll tag leadership for clarifications.
Eli (SRE): Will Dedicated include EU GPU capacity for customers needing data residency? our infra team is planning hookups.
Maya (Head of Strategy): Short answer: yes, EU Dedicated is a priority for Q3. We're validating region-specific kernels and infra configs now.
Asha (CEO): We're also prioritizing Private (VPC/on‑prem) pilots for regulated finance & health customers — solutions-eng will start outreach next week.
Marco (CTO): Tech detail: routing policy work next sprint should cut tail latency ~10-20% for longer sequences by improving kernel selection fallback.
Priya (VP Product): To clarify positioning vs cloud AI endpoints: we don't compete on raw model count. We compete on predictable inference economics + rollouts + private deployments. That's our one-liner to product teams.
Sam (Sales): For enterprise decks: can we get a single sentence differentiator we can use externally?
Maya (Head of Strategy): Use: "Redwood makes inference predictable and economical across hosted, reserved, and private deployments." Keep it short in slides.
Jordan (PM): Any change to pricing cadence or public pricing? customers ask about reserved discounts.
Priya (VP Product): No public pricing change this quarter. We're testing reserved commit discounts with pilot accounts — will share guidance after pilots.
Eli (SRE): When you say "predictable" — what metrics should eng teams cite? p50/p95 latency, token cost, and successful rollout rate?
Marco (CTO): Yes. Also include model-version rollback time and cache hit rate for cost controls. We'll add those metrics to the per-route dashboards.
Sam (Sales): Do we ever call out competitors by name in GTM? Some reps want direct comparisons.
Asha (CEO): Not in public-facing collateral. Internally we map competitor capabilities and gaps, but outward messaging focuses on our customer outcomes (cost, latency, control).
Eli (SRE): Quick ops question: how do canary rollouts work with Dedicated? we need docs for SRE runbooks.
Marco (CTO): Canary is cross-deployment: small traffic slice, automated quality evals against prompt sets, and automatic fallback to previous variant if regressions detected. Docs are being updated in eng-runbooks.
Jordan (PM): Follow-up: can leadership share the customer signals that would push us to prioritize new features (e.g., model quantization tool, L2 cache)?
Maya (Head of Strategy): Primary signals: repeated customer asks, measurable unit-cost impact for high-volume use cases, and integration blockers for enterprise deals.
Sam (Sales): Noted. will add to deal playbook.
Priya (VP Product): We're also adding a simple decision rubric to the roadmap doc — will post link in this thread when ready.
Eli (SRE): tiny ask: can we get a one-page FWIW doc on "why Redwood" for new hires — technical bullets?
Maya (Head of Strategy): Good idea — Priya and Marco can put together a 1-pager: mission, runtime differentiators, and top 5 technical wins.
Asha (CEO): Thanks everyone. appreciate concise Qs like this — helps shape priorities.
ops-bot: Recording and slides uploaded: https://redwood.example.com/all-hands/2166543210 :white_check_mark:
Sam (Sales): +1 to the 1-pager — will use in calls.
Jordan (PM): Will follow up if we need more specifics on metrics/thresholds.
Maya (Head of Strategy): Closing this thread at EOD unless more major asks. Thanks!
